overview.oneLineTake: The Fed's hawkish pivot into an oil-shocked, politically charged environment has triggered a bond-market revolt and equity drawdown, pushing markets into a rising-volatility regime with acute policy and credit risk.
themes: Hawkish Fed restart: First hike since 2023 with Warsh signaling more to come, directly defying Trump's demands for sub-1% rates and sparking a policy-credibility crisis
Bond-market revolt: 10-year Treasury yield surged to 5% (highest since 2007), mortgage rates neared 7%, and long-dated corporate issuance is freezing up
Energy-inflation feedback loop: Iran war, Saudi pipeline attacks, and diesel shortages are amplifying inflation just as the Fed tightens, creating a stagflationary impulse
Cross-asset de-risking: Dow plunged 600+ points, analysts are slashing S&P 500 targets, and the dollar is spiking as global liquidity recedes
Consumer/housing stress: Homebuilder sentiment hit a 12-month low, hedge funds are stepping up shorts in consumer names, and retail spending is being fueled by savings drawdowns
risks: Disorderly bond-market move and private-credit stress (US private credit default rate hit a record 6.3%; Turkish funds defaulted on redemptions)
Fed independence under active political siege, raising tail-risk of erratic policy
Escalating Middle East supply shocks that could spike oil further despite the Fed's inflation fight
